correctness.rationale: For every 1<=a<=b, coarea reduces norm inequalities to cuts; the cut Bernoulli identity plus integer cross-cut inequalities proves sharp two-sided mean centering. One-sided centering follows from the exact column sum of the l1 projection I-J/b and Jensen. An explicit nonnegative spectral decomposition of all heat cross-edge differences gives the upper bound; a singleton in the larger part attains it at every time. Direct differentiation gives the sharp degree-imbalance threshold and unique peak. Exact rational verification covers representative sizes and witnesses, with no finite-to-infinite inference.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary theorems address heat gradient/curvature, supremum-edge Lipschitz norms, or graph edge-gradient estimates at p>1. Neither the exact unweighted biclique edge-variation semigroup norm nor the sharp bipartite cross-difference centering inequality was identified there. Previously obtained Lipschitz-profile constants are disclosed as a different-seminorm predecessor, not counted as original. Search limitations and an implicit-antecedent risk remain.
residual_risks: An old exact formula for a cross-difference centering operator may be published under Gini dispersion, matrix mean-deviation or polyhedral operator-norm terminology.

The previously known Lipschitz numerical profile is identical on bicliques, so originality is limited to proving the distinct variation norm and its centering mechanism.

value.rationale: Exact time-resolved l1 graph-gradient stability over all biclique sizes is a natural sharp BV invariant; the sharp new cross-difference centering lemma is independently applicable. The nonexpansivity boundary and asymptotic amplification law quantify transient instability not entailed by l2 contractivity or previously established l-infinity Lipschitz estimates. The result does not rely on arbitrary finite parameter slicing.
